hints: Think about the two separate ideas here. First, does mammalian blood stay inside vessels all the time, or does it spill out to bathe the tissues directly?
Second, count how many times blood goes through the heart in one full trip. Remember mammals have a pulmonary circuit to the lungs and a systemic circuit to the body.
walkthrough:
**Check Open or Closed**

Think of closed as blood always staying in pipes. In mammals, blood is always confined inside arteries, capillaries and veins, it never bathes tissues directly. That means closed, not open.

Open systems are found in insects and most molluscs, not mammals.

**Check Single or Double**

Think of double as two loops with the heart in the middle. Mammals have one loop to the lungs (pulmonary circulation) and a second loop to the rest of the body (systemic circulation).

Blood passes through the heart twice for each complete circuit, once on the right side and once on the left side. That means double, not single.

**Put Them Together**

Closed plus double gives the mammalian pattern. This keeps blood pressure high and keeps oxygenated and deoxygenated blood separate, which is perfect for active, warm-blooded mammals.

options.A: Open is wrong because mammalian blood never leaves the vessels to bathe tissues directly.
options.B: Correct, because blood stays in vessels (closed) and passes through the heart twice per circuit via pulmonary and systemic loops (double).
options.C: Single is wrong because fish have single circulation, while mammals have two circuits with the heart in the centre.
options.D: Both parts are wrong for mammals, open and single describes a simpler system, not the high-pressure mammalian system.
